children.text:
[Oṃ bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ śṛṇuyāma devāḥ bhadraṃ paśyemākṣabhir yajatrāḥ |
sthirair aṅgais tuṣṭuvāṃsas tanūbhir vyaśema devahitaṃ yadāyuḥ |
svasti na indro vṛddhaśravāḥ svasti naḥ pūṣā viśvavedāḥ |
svasti nas tārkṣyo 'riṣṭanemiḥ svasti no bṛhaspatir dadhātu |
Oṃ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ |]
children.translated_text:
[<s>Oṃ</s>. May we hear what is auspicious with our ears, O gods; may we see what is auspicious with our eyes, O worshipful ones.
With firm limbs, with bodies offering praise, may we enjoy the lifespan allotted by the gods.
May <s>Indra</s> of great renown grant us well-being; may <s>Pūṣan</s>, the all-knowing, grant us well-being.
May <s>Tārkṣya</s> of unimpaired rim grant us well-being; may <s>Bṛhaspati</s> grant us well-being.
<s>Oṃ</s>. Peace, peace, peace.]

children.text: oṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>.

children.text: athāśvalāyano bhagavantaṃ parameṣṭhinam upasametyovāca |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Āśvalāyana</s>, approaching the Lord <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), said:

children.text: adhīhi bhagavan brahmavidyāṃ variṣṭhāṃ sadā sadbhiḥ sevyamānāṃ nigūḍhām |
children.translated_text: Teach me, O Lord, the supreme knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, the most excellent, always pursued by the wise, hidden —

children.text: yathācirāt [yayācirāt] sarvapāpaṃ vyapohya parātparaṃ puruṣaṃ yāti vidvān ||1||
children.translated_text: by which a wise person, having quickly cast off all sins, attains the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Being) who is beyond the beyond. ||1||

children.text: tasmai sa hovāca pitāmahaś ca śraddhā-bhakti-dhyāna-yogād avaihi |
children.translated_text: To him the Grandfather (<s>Brahmā</s>) said: Know [this] through faith, devotion, meditation, and <s>yoga</s>;

children.text: na karmaṇā na prajayā dhanena tyāgenaike amṛtatvam ānaśuḥ ||2||
children.translated_text: not by works, not by progeny, not by wealth — by renunciation alone have some attained immortality. ||2||

children.text: pareṇa nākaṃ nihitaṃ guhāyāṃ vibhrājate yad yatayo viśanti |
children.translated_text: Beyond heaven, established in the cave [of the heart], that which shines — into which the ascetics enter;

children.text: vedānta-vijñānasuniścitārthāḥ saṃnyāsayogād yatayaḥ śuddhasattvāḥ ||3||
children.translated_text: those ascetics of purified being, whose understanding is firmly established through <s>Vedānta</s> knowledge, [attain it] through the <s>yoga</s> of renunciation (<s>saṃnyāsa</s>). ||3||

children.text: te brahmalokeṣu parāntakāle parāmṛtāḥ [parāmṛtāt] parimucyanti sarve |
children.translated_text: They, in the <s>Brahma</s>-worlds, at the final hour, being beyond death, are all completely liberated.

children.text: viviktadeśe ca sukhāsanasthaḥ śuciḥ samagrīvaśiraḥśarīraḥ ||4||
children.translated_text: Seated comfortably in a secluded place, pure, with neck, head, and body held erect, ||4||

children.text: antyāśramasthaḥ sakalendriyāṇi nirudhya bhaktyā svaguruṃ praṇamya |
children.translated_text: dwelling in the last <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life), having restrained all the senses, bowing with devotion to one's own guru,

children.text: hṛtpuṇḍarīkaṃ virajaṃ viśuddhaṃ vicintya madhye viṣadam [viśadaṃ] viśokam ||5||
children.translated_text: contemplating the lotus of the heart — stainless, pure, clear in its center, free from sorrow, ||5||

children.text: acintyam avyaktam anantarūpaṃ śivaṃ praśāntam amṛtaṃ brahmayonim |
children.translated_text: unthinkable, unmanifest, of infinite form, auspicious, tranquil, immortal, the source of <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: tam ādimadhyāntavihīnam ekaṃ vibhuṃ cidānandam arūpam adbhutam ||6||
children.translated_text: that One — devoid of beginning, middle, and end, all-pervading, of the nature of consciousness and bliss, formless, wondrous, ||6||

children.text: umāsahāyaṃ parameśvaraṃ prabhuṃ trilocanaṃ nīlakaṇṭhaṃ praśāntam |
children.translated_text: accompanied by <s>Umā</s>, the supreme Lord, the ruler, three-eyed, blue-throated, tranquil —

children.text: dhyātvā munirgacchati bhūtayoniṃ samastasākṣiṃ tamasaḥ parastāt ||7||
children.translated_text: meditating upon Him, the sage attains the source of all beings, the witness of all, who is beyond darkness. ||7||

children.text: sa brahmā sa śivaḥ sendraḥ so 'kṣaraḥ paramaḥ svarāṭ |
children.translated_text: He is <s>Brahmā</s>, He is <s>Śiva</s>, He is <s>Indra</s>, He is the imperishable, the supreme, the self-luminous;

children.text: sa eva viṣṇuḥ sa prāṇaḥ sa kālo 'gniḥ sa candramāḥ ||8||
children.translated_text: He alone is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, He is <s>Prāṇa</s> (the life-breath), He is Time, He is Fire, He is the Moon. ||8||

children.text: sa eva sarvaṃ yad bhūtaṃ yac ca bhavyaṃ sanātanam |
children.translated_text: He alone is everything that has been and everything that shall be, the eternal;

children.text: jñātvā taṃ mṛtyum atyeti nānyaḥ panthā vimuktaye ||9||
children.translated_text: having known Him, one transcends death — there is no other path to liberation. ||9||

children.text: sarvabhūtastham ātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani |
children.translated_text: Seeing the Self in all beings and all beings in the Self,

children.text: saṃpaśyan brahma paramaṃ yāti nānyena hetunā ||10||
children.translated_text: beholding the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, one attains [it] — by no other means. ||10||

children.text: ātmānam araṇiṃ kṛtvā praṇavaṃ cottarāraṇim |
children.translated_text: Making the self the lower fire-stick (<s>araṇi</s>) and <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>) the upper fire-stick,

children.text: jñānanirmathanābhyāsāt pāpaṃ [pāśaṃ] dahati paṇḍitaḥ ||11||
children.translated_text: through the repeated churning of knowledge, the wise one burns away sin [or bondage]. ||11||

children.text: sa eva māyāparimohitātmā śarīram āsthāya karoti sarvam |
children.translated_text: He alone, the Self deluded by <s>māyā</s>, assuming a body, does everything;

children.text: striyannapānādivicitrabhogaiḥ sa eva jāgrat paritṛptim eti ||12||
children.translated_text: through the various enjoyments of women, food, drink, and the rest, He alone in the waking state attains satisfaction. ||12||

children.text: svapna [svapne] sa jīvaḥ sukhaduḥkhabhoktā svamāyayā kalpitajīvaloke |
children.translated_text: In dream, that <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), the experiencer of happiness and suffering, in the world of the <s>jīva</s> created by his own <s>māyā</s>,

children.text: suṣuptikāle sakale vilīne tamo 'bhibhūtaḥ sukharūpam eti ||13||
children.translated_text: in the state of deep sleep, when all is dissolved, overcome by darkness, he attains the state of bliss. ||13||

children.text: punaśca janmāntarakarmayogāt sa eva jīvaḥ svapiti prabuddhaḥ |
children.translated_text: And again, by the force of <s>karma</s> from other births, that same <s>jīva</s>, awakened, sleeps [again];

children.text: puratraye krīḍati yaśca jīvas tatas tu jātaṃ sakalaṃ vicitram ||14||
children.translated_text: that <s>jīva</s> who plays in the three cities [of waking, dream, and deep sleep] — from him has arisen all this manifold [creation]. ||14||

children.text: dhāramānandam akhaṇḍabodhaṃ yasmiṃl layaṃ yāti puratrayaṃ ca ||14*||
children.translated_text: The support, the bliss, the undivided consciousness — into whom the three cities dissolve. ||14*||

children.text: etasmāj jāyate prāṇo manaḥ sarvendriyāṇi ca |
children.translated_text: From this [<s>Brahman</s>] are born <s>Prāṇa</s> (life-breath), mind, and all the sense organs,

children.text: khaṃ vāyur jyotir āpaḥ pṛthivī viśvasya dhāriṇī ||15||
children.translated_text: space, air, light, water, and earth — the supporter of all. ||15||

children.text: yat paraṃ brahma sarvātmā viśvasyāyatanaṃ mahat |
children.translated_text: That which is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the Self of all, the great abode of the universe,

children.text: sūkṣmāt sūkṣmataraṃ nityaṃ tat tvam eva tvam eva tat ||16||
children.translated_text: subtler than the subtle, eternal — that is you yourself; you yourself are that. ||16||

children.text: jāgratsvapnasuṣuptyādiprapañcaṃ yat prakāśate |
children.translated_text: The phenomenal world that shines forth in waking, dream, deep sleep, and the other states —

children.text: tad brahmāham iti jñātvā sarvabandhaiḥ pramucyate ||17||
children.translated_text: knowing 'I am that <s>Brahman</s>,' one is freed from all bonds. ||17||

children.text: triṣu dhāmasu yad bhogyaṃ bhoktā bhogaś ca yad bhavet |
children.translated_text: In the three abodes, that which is the enjoyed, the enjoyer, and the enjoyment,

children.text: tebhyo vilakṣaṇaḥ sākṣī cinmātro 'haṃ sadā śivaḥ ||18||
children.translated_text: different from all these, I am the witness, pure consciousness alone, ever auspicious (<s>Śiva</s>). ||18||

children.text: mayy eva sakalaṃ jātaṃ mayi sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam |
children.translated_text: In me alone is everything born, in me is everything established,

children.text: mayi sarvaṃl layaṃ yāti tad brahmādvayam asmy aham ||19||
children.translated_text: in me does everything dissolve — I am that non-dual <s>Brahman</s>. ||19||

children.text: [iti] prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first section.

children.text: aṇor aṇiyān aham eva tadvan mahān ahaṃ viśvam ahaṃ vicitram |
children.translated_text: I am smaller than the smallest and likewise I am the greatest; I am the manifold universe;

children.text: purātano 'haṃ puruṣo 'ham īśo hiraṇmayo 'haṃ śivarūpam asmi ||20||
children.translated_text: I am the ancient one, I am the <s>Puruṣa</s>, I am the Lord, I am golden in form, I am of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>. ||20||

children.text: apāṇipādo 'ham acintyaśaktiḥ paśyāmy acakṣuḥ sa śṛṇomy akarṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: I am without hands and feet, of inconceivable power; I see without eyes, I hear without ears;

children.text: ahaṃ vijānāmi viviktarūpo na cāsti vettā mama cit sadāham ||21||
children.translated_text: I know, being of distinct form — and there is no knower of me; I am ever pure consciousness. ||21||

children.text: vedair anekair aham eva vedyo vedāntakṛd vedavid eva cāham |
children.translated_text: By many <s>Vedas</s> I alone am to be known; I am the maker of the <s>Vedānta</s> and the knower of the <s>Vedas</s>.

children.text: na puṇyapāpe mama nāsti nāśo na janma dehendriyabuddhir asti ||22||
children.translated_text: Neither merit nor sin is mine; there is no destruction for me, no birth, no body, no senses, no intellect. ||22||

children.text: na bhūmir āpo na ca vahnir asti na cānilo me 'sti na cāmbaraṃ ca |
children.translated_text: There is no earth, no water, no fire for me; there is no wind, nor is there space for me.

children.text: evaṃ viditvā paramātmarūpaṃ guhāśayaṃ niṣkalam advitīyam ||23||
children.translated_text: Having known thus the nature of the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), dwelling in the cave [of the heart], without parts, without a second, ||23||

children.text: samastasākṣiṃ sadasadvihīnaṃ prayāti śuddhaṃ paramātmarūpam ||23*||
children.translated_text: the witness of all, beyond existence and non-existence — one attains the pure nature of the Supreme Self. ||23*||

children.text: yaḥ śatarūdrīyam adhīte so 'gnipūto bhavati sa vāyupūto bhavati, sa ātmapūto bhavati sa surāpānāt pūto bhavati sa brahmahatyātpūto bhavati sa suvarṇasteyāt pūto bhavati sa kṛtyākṛtyāt pūto bhavati tasmād avimuktam āśrito bhavaty āśramī sarvadā sakṛd vā japet |
children.translated_text: Whoever recites the <s>Śatarudrīya</s> becomes purified by fire; he becomes purified by wind; he becomes purified in the Self; he becomes purified from the drinking of liquor; he becomes purified from the killing of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; he becomes purified from the theft of gold; he becomes purified from deeds done and undone. Therefore, he becomes one who has taken refuge in the <s>Avimukta</s> [<s>Kāśī</s>], an <s>āśramin</s> (one established in a stage of life). He should recite it always, or even once.

children.text: anena jñānam āpnoti saṃsārārṇavanāśanam |
children.translated_text: By this one obtains knowledge that destroys the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence).

children.text: tasmād evaṃ viditvainaṃ kaivalyaṃ padam [phalam] aśnute |
children.translated_text: Therefore, having known this thus, one attains <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute liberation) — the supreme state [fruit],

children.text: kaivalyaṃ padam [phalam] aśnute ||24||
children.translated_text: one attains <s>kaivalya</s>, the supreme state [fruit]. ||24||

children.text: ity atharvavede kaivalyopaniṣat samāptā ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Kaivalyopaniṣad</s> of the <s>Atharvaveda</s>.

children.text: oṃ tat sat
children.translated_text: Oṃ tat sat.
